title: Psilocybin could kick-start anorexia recovery, early results suggest
excerpt: An active ingredient in magic mushrooms, psilocybin has shown early promise for treating eating disorders
content_html:
It was 2022, and Christina was running out of options. The Londoner, then age 34, was desperate to fix her anorexia nervosa, even as the disease consumed her. After six years of battling the disease, she’d tried various forms of behavioral therapy and months of in-patient care, but nothing stuck. At its worst, the disease was preventing her from sleeping and zapping so much energy that she was unable to climb her stairs or brush her teeth. She needed a radical fix.

“You become your anorexia,” says Christina (a pseudonym to protect her privacy). “You have no life around it. You don’t laugh. You don’t smile. You don’t find joy in anything,” she recalls. Her relationships suffered, and she almost lost her job and house. 

Eventually, a frantic Google search for “cures for anorexia” alerted her to a clinical trial for the psychedelic psilocybin—an active ingredient in magic mushrooms—as a treatment for the disease. She signed up.

“I genuinely believe, had I not done that trial, I would either be stuck in a hospital loop, or I wouldn't be here today,” she says. “It saved my life.”

Life with an eating disorder can turn the mind and body into a prison. Intrusive, never-ending thought spirals drive compulsive behaviors such as binging, overexercising, purging and restrictive eating. Conventional psychiatric treatments, such as cognitive-behavioral therapy or antidepressants, work in only about half of patients. People with anorexia are more than 18 times more likely to die by suicide than the general population—the highest mortality rate of any psychiatric disorder.

For decades, researchers have searched for more effective therapies, but progress has been slow. Now scientists are turning to more unorthodox approaches, including psilocybin therapy.

Research-wise, it’s early days. Still, 2026 could be a tipping point for psychedelics. The Trump administration has pushed U.S. drug regulators to embrace the field and fund studies into using these drugs to treat mental health conditions. In psilocybin’s case, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration could approve the psychedelic to treat depression or eating disorders within five years, predicts Robin Carhart-Harris, Ralph Metzner Distinguished Professor of Neurology and Psychiatry at the University of California, San Francisco.

“Psilocybin therapy has the potential to stop a lot of unnecessary suffering,” says Jennifer Danby, a psychotherapist who specializes in eating disorders. 

Inside a Psilocybin Therapy Session

Psilocybin has shown potential to treat post-traumatic stress disorder, depression and other psychiatric illnesses. Carhart-Harris says that there was an “intuition” that the psychedelic could break down mental barriers in anorexia, too. 

This inkling, combined with the broader lack of effective treatments, inspired a small pilot trial involving 21 women. The participants had lived with anorexia nervosa for an average of 11 years. In that study, published last month, Danby and her colleagues found that psilocybin, combined with talk therapy, reduced anorexia symptoms and increased participants’ motivation to change. 

The data follow another small study, published in 2023 in Nature Medicine, that found that four out of 10 patients with the condition experienced significant drops in their eating disorder scores after a single dose of psilocybin. If confirmed in larger trials, these results suggest that psilocybin therapy could kick-start anorexia recovery and provide relief.

In 2022 Christina joined the trial. Over six weeks, the group received three doses of oral psilocybin—first one milligram and then two 25-mg doses, each two weeks apart—alongside intensive talk therapy before and after dosing. There were few adverse events, and only one person withdrew from the study; however, another participant attempted suicide twice, events that the research team says were unrelated to the trial.

This psilocybin therapy differed from typical eating disorder treatments in a couple of notable ways: there was no nutritional intervention or focus on gaining weight, and the researchers didn’t see a meaningful change in participants’ body mass index. Instead they focused on self-compassion and involving family members for support.

The researchers followed up with the participants two weeks, three months, six months and then one year after the trial. They found that, on average, the severity of the participants’ symptoms were reduced. After three months, half of the participants had scores on a measure of eating disorder symptoms comparable to those of someone without a diagnosis. And participants reported increased motivation to recover that lasted up to a year after the trial ended.

“These are people who’ve tried everything, and nothing’s worked,” says Carhart-Harris, who co-authored the study. Getting half of them in remission at three months was “impressive.” 

“The results of this study are profound,” says Claire Finkelstein, a clinical psychologist at Swinburne University of Technology in Australia, who was not involved in the trial. “But the data, while promising, has shown us that it isn’t working for everyone. We need more research to learn who it helps, why and how to improve treatment for those who aren’t responding.”

For 41-year-old Katharine, a participant in the trial who had been living with severe anorexia for 15 years and requested that only her first name be used in this story, psilocybin therapy wasn’t a “magic wand.” But over time, she says, the trial “cracked me open in a way.”

“I still struggle sometimes, but since the trial, I wouldn’t define myself as someone who is anorexic anymore,” she says.

To David Hellerstein, a professor of clinical psychiatry at the Columbia University Irving Medical Center, who was not involved in the study, the findings are “modestly encouraging,” but there are caveats. There was no control group, so it’s hard to know if psilocybin made the difference.

Still, so few effective treatments for anorexia exist that any positive signal is meaningful, the trial researchers say. “People have likened anorexia to a slow suicide,” Carhart-Harris says. “To have that flip to feeling like ‘I want to live and be healthy’ is massive.”

Some people with eating disorders aren’t waiting for drug approvals or new regulation; they’re already self-medicating with psychedelics through underground channels. Some of these have seen positive results, while others have experienced psychological turmoil.

“People’s expectations and hopes have far outstripped the evidence,” warns Hellerstein, adding that more rigorous studies are critical. 

For now, “there is hope” for people with eating disorders, says study co-author Hannah Douglass, a researcher at Imperial College London, who emphasizes that evidence-based care exists. “You can absolutely recover without psychedelics.”

Shaking the “Snow Globe”

As it stands, recovery can be brutal. Eating disorders are particularly challenging to treat, in part because they are a “survival strategy,” Danby says—a coping mechanism for overwhelming situations. “The symptoms of anorexia are a language of pain,” explains Danby’s colleague Meg Vardy, a researcher and chairperson of the New Zealand–based eating disorder charity JourneyED Eating Disorder Support Aotearoa (the Māori name for New Zealand). The condition is rarely just about food or weight, but “something going on underneath.”

Anorexia can provide comfort, control, a sense of order and something to fixate on, says trial participant Katharine. “It is very difficult to let go of because it is filling a hole.” 

A starving or underweight brain also tends to become more rigid, “black and white” in its thinking, sensitive to fear and closed to change. Eating disorders are somewhat like obsessive-compulsive disorder or substance use disorder and involve brain circuits that are very resistant to intervention, Hellerstein says.

Both animal and human studies suggest psychedelics could change brain function and increase cognitive flexibility, as well as emotional connectedness—features that tend to be impaired in people with eating disorders.

Carhart-Harris likens psilocybin therapy to “shaking a snow globe.” The idea is to shake up and weaken potentially problematic thought patterns and introduce opportunities to do things differently, he says. In animal studies, psychedelics appear to induce a window of neuroplasticity, making the brain more malleable. “It can be an opportunity to regain agency [and] self-determination and not be a slave to habits that are strongly ingrained,” he says.

That plasticity can go either way, however—positive change, a relapse risk or a period of destabilization that’s especially dangerous for anorexia, Finkelstein cautions. Combining the drug with talk therapy may be critical to its success: this isn't a “magic bullet,” Vardy says.

Bypassing the “Thinking Brain”

Katharine, who spent 15 years in and out of hospitals because of her anorexia, says her psilocybin therapy sessions were “completely extraordinary.” 

During one dosing, she had a vision of skating on a lake: “My mind was on the sidelines, saying to my body, ‘You can just be free now. I’m not going to hold you back. Just go; fly,’” she says. “And there was this feeling of complete release. My body was free.”

“Anorexia keeps you small in many ways,” she says. “I reconnected with how it felt to be a human and alive and sad and happy and nourished. [In the trial], I realized that I am the source of my healing, my power and my own strength.”

Psilocybin therapy is not without risks, and experts caution that it shouldn’t happen without specialized support. The process can be transcendent—and terrifying.

Trial participant Christina was “very nervous” going in, she recalls. She expected visions of “fluffy clouds, unicorns and rainbows.” Instead the sessions felt horrific.

“All I could see was blood everywhere,” she says. “The therapists’ faces morphed, and I felt like I was surrounded by monsters. I thought, ‘Oh, my god, what have I done?’”

The drug’s action is “psychologically agitating,” Carhart-Harris says, and it can surface unpleasant content, thoughts or memories. It requires courage, he says, but can be incredibly transformative. “You can let go of these demons.”

Psychedelics also work in a somatic way, meaning they bypass the “thinking brain” to allow physical sensations to help guide emotional processing, Danby explains. That can be useful for eating disorders because people often disconnect from feelings such as hunger, thirst, fatigue and cold.

Despite her uncomfortable experiences on the drug, Christina says, the trial was life-changing. She started listening to her bodily cues again, taking risks and reengaging with life.

“In terms of the quality of my life, it’s unrecognizable,” Christina says. “I can feel again. I attribute 95 percent of where I am today to the trial.”

sentences.en: Carhart-Harris says that there was an “intuition” that the psychedelic could break down mental barriers in anorexia, too.
sentences.zh: 卡哈特-哈里斯说，人们有一种“直觉”，认为迷幻药也可以打破厌食症的心理障碍。

blocks.html_en: This inkling, combined with the broader lack of effective treatments, inspired a small pilot trial involving 21 women. The participants had lived with anorexia nervosa for an average of 11 years. In that study, published last month, Danby and her colleagues found that psilocybin, combined with talk therapy, reduced anorexia symptoms and increased participants’ motivation to change.

sentences.en: This inkling, combined with the broader lack of effective treatments, inspired a small pilot trial involving 21 women.
sentences.zh: 这一暗示，加上更广泛缺乏有效治疗方法，激发了一项涉及 21 名女性的小型试点试验。

sentences.en: The participants had lived with anorexia nervosa for an average of 11 years.
sentences.zh: 参与者平均患有神经性厌食症 11 年。

sentences.en: In that study, published last month, Danby and her colleagues found that psilocybin, combined with talk therapy, reduced anorexia symptoms and increased participants’ motivation to change.
sentences.zh: 在上个月发表的这项研究中，丹比和她的同事发现裸盖菇素与谈话疗法相结合，可以减轻厌食症状并增加参与者改变的动力。

blocks.html_en: The data follow another small study, published in 2023 in Nature Medicine, that found that four out of 10 patients with the condition experienced significant drops in their eating disorder scores after a single dose of psilocybin. If confirmed in larger trials, these results suggest that psilocybin therapy could kick-start anorexia recovery and provide relief.

sentences.en: The data follow another small study, published in 2023 in Nature Medicine, that found that four out of 10 patients with the condition experienced significant drops in their eating disorder scores after a single dose of psilocybin.
sentences.zh: 该数据是在 2023 年《自然医学》杂志上发表的另一项小型研究之后发现的，该研究发现，每 10 名患有这种疾病的患者中，有 4 人在服用单剂量裸盖菇素后，其饮食失调评分显着下降。

sentences.en: If confirmed in larger trials, these results suggest that psilocybin therapy could kick-start anorexia recovery and provide relief.
sentences.zh: 如果在更大规模的试验中得到证实，这些结果表明裸盖菇素疗法可以启动厌食症的恢复并提供缓解。

blocks.html_en: In 2022 Christina joined the trial. Over six weeks, the group received three doses of oral psilocybin—first one milligram and then two 25-mg doses, each two weeks apart—alongside intensive talk therapy before and after dosing. There were few adverse events, and only one person withdrew from the study; however, another participant attempted suicide twice, events that the research team says were unrelated to the trial.

sentences.en: In 2022 Christina joined the trial.
sentences.zh: 2022 年，克里斯蒂娜加入了审判。

sentences.en: Over six weeks, the group received three doses of oral psilocybin—first one milligram and then two 25-mg doses, each two weeks apart—alongside intensive talk therapy before and after dosing.
sentences.zh: 在六周的时间里，该小组接受了三剂口服裸盖菇素——首先是一毫克，然后是两剂 25 毫克，每剂间隔两周——同时在给药前后进行强化谈话治疗。

sentences.en: There were few adverse events, and only one person withdrew from the study; however, another participant attempted suicide twice, events that the research team says were unrelated to the trial.
sentences.zh: 不良事件很少，只有 1 人退出研究；然而，另一名参与者两次试图自杀，研究小组称这些事件与试验无关。

blocks.html_en: This psilocybin therapy differed from typical eating disorder treatments in a couple of notable ways: there was no nutritional intervention or focus on gaining weight, and the researchers didn’t see a meaningful change in participants’ body mass index. Instead they focused on self-compassion and involving family members for support.

sentences.en: This psilocybin therapy differed from typical eating disorder treatments in a couple of notable ways: there was no nutritional intervention or focus on gaining weight, and the researchers didn’t see a meaningful change in participants’ body mass index.
sentences.zh: 这种裸盖菇素疗法与典型的饮食失调疗法有几个显着的不同：没有营养干预或专注于增加体重，研究人员没有看到参与者的体重指数发生有意义的变化。

sentences.en: Instead they focused on self-compassion and involving family members for support.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们专注于自我同情并让家庭成员寻求支持。

blocks.html_en: The researchers followed up with the participants two weeks, three months, six months and then one year after the trial. They found that, on average, the severity of the participants’ symptoms were reduced. After three months, half of the participants had scores on a measure of eating disorder symptoms comparable to those of someone without a diagnosis. And participants reported increased motivation to recover that lasted up to a year after the trial ended.

sentences.en: The researchers followed up with the participants two weeks, three months, six months and then one year after the trial.
sentences.zh: 研究人员在试验后两周、三个月、六个月和一年对参与者进行了随访。

sentences.en: They found that, on average, the severity of the participants’ symptoms were reduced.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，平均而言，参与者症状的严重程度有所减轻。

sentences.en: After three months, half of the participants had scores on a measure of eating disorder symptoms comparable to those of someone without a diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 三个月后，一半的参与者在饮食失调症状测量方面的得分与未诊断的人相当。

sentences.en: And participants reported increased motivation to recover that lasted up to a year after the trial ended.
sentences.zh: 参与者报告说，在试验结束后，恢复的动力持续了一年。

blocks.html_en: “These are people who’ve tried everything, and nothing’s worked,” says Carhart-Harris, who co-authored the study. Getting half of them in remission at three months was “impressive.”

sentences.en: “These are people who’ve tried everything, and nothing’s worked,” says Carhart-Harris, who co-authored the study.
sentences.zh: 该研究的合著者卡哈特-哈里斯说：“这些人已经尝试了一切，但没有任何效果。”

sentences.en: Getting half of them in remission at three months was “impressive.”
sentences.zh: 其中一半人在三个月后病情得到缓解，这“令人印象深刻”。

blocks.html_en: “The results of this study are profound,” says Claire Finkelstein, a clinical psychologist at Swinburne University of Technology in Australia, who was not involved in the trial. “But the data, while promising, has shown us that it isn’t working for everyone. We need more research to learn who it helps, why and how to improve treatment for those who aren’t responding.”

sentences.en: “The results of this study are profound,” says Claire Finkelstein, a clinical psychologist at Swinburne University of Technology in Australia, who was not involved in the trial.
sentences.zh: “这项研究的结果意义深远，”澳大利亚斯威本科技大学临床心理学家克莱尔·芬克尔斯坦（Claire Finkelstein）说，她没有参与这项试验。

sentences.en: “But the data, while promising, has shown us that it isn’t working for everyone.
sentences.zh: “但数据虽然很有希望，但也向我们表明，它并不适合所有人。

sentences.en: We need more research to learn who it helps, why and how to improve treatment for those who aren’t responding.”
sentences.zh: 我们需要更多的研究来了解它对谁有帮助、为什么以及如何改善对那些没有反应的人的治疗。”

blocks.html_en: For 41-year-old Katharine, a participant in the trial who had been living with severe anorexia for 15 years and requested that only her first name be used in this story, psilocybin therapy wasn’t a “magic wand.” But over time, she says, the trial “cracked me open in a way.”

sentences.en: For 41-year-old Katharine, a participant in the trial who had been living with severe anorexia for 15 years and requested that only her first name be used in this story, psilocybin therapy wasn’t a “magic wand.”
sentences.zh: 41 岁的试验参与者凯瑟琳 (Katharine) 患有严重厌食症 15 年，并要求在本文中只使用她的名字，对于她来说，裸盖菇素疗法并不是一根“魔杖”。

sentences.en: But over time, she says, the trial “cracked me open in a way.”
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，她说，这次审判“在某种程度上让我心碎了”。

blocks.html_en: “I still struggle sometimes, but since the trial, I wouldn’t define myself as someone who is anorexic anymore,” she says.

sentences.en: “I still struggle sometimes, but since the trial, I wouldn’t define myself as someone who is anorexic anymore,” she says.
sentences.zh: “有时我仍然会挣扎，但自从审判以来，我不会再将自己定义为厌食症患者，”她说。

blocks.html_en: To David Hellerstein, a professor of clinical psychiatry at the Columbia University Irving Medical Center, who was not involved in the study, the findings are “modestly encouraging,” but there are caveats. There was no control group, so it’s hard to know if psilocybin made the difference.

sentences.en: To David Hellerstein, a professor of clinical psychiatry at the Columbia University Irving Medical Center, who was not involved in the study, the findings are “modestly encouraging,” but there are caveats.
sentences.zh: 哥伦比亚大学欧文医学中心临床精神病学教授大卫·海勒斯坦（David Hellerstein）并未参与这项研究，他认为，这些发现“有点令人鼓舞”，但也有一些警告。

sentences.en: There was no control group, so it’s hard to know if psilocybin made the difference.
sentences.zh: 由于没有对照组，因此很难知道裸盖菇素是否会产生影响。

blocks.html_en: Still, so few effective treatments for anorexia exist that any positive signal is meaningful, the trial researchers say. “People have likened anorexia to a slow suicide,” Carhart-Harris says. “To have that flip to feeling like ‘I want to live and be healthy’ is massive.”

sentences.en: Still, so few effective treatments for anorexia exist that any positive signal is meaningful, the trial researchers say.
sentences.zh: 试验研究人员表示，尽管如此，针对厌食症的有效治疗方法仍然很少，任何积极的信号都是有意义的。

sentences.en: “People have likened anorexia to a slow suicide,” Carhart-Harris says.
sentences.zh: “人们把厌食症比作慢性自杀，”卡哈特-哈里斯说。

sentences.en: “To have that flip to feeling like ‘I want to live and be healthy’ is massive.”
sentences.zh: “那种‘我想要活下去并且保持健康’的感觉是巨大的。”

blocks.html_en: Some people with eating disorders aren’t waiting for drug approvals or new regulation; they’re already self-medicating with psychedelics through underground channels. Some of these have seen positive results, while others have experienced psychological turmoil.

sentences.en: Some people with eating disorders aren’t waiting for drug approvals or new regulation; they’re already self-medicating with psychedelics through underground channels.
sentences.zh: 一些患有饮食失调的人并没有等待药物批准或新法规；他们正在等待。他们已经通过地下渠道使用迷幻药进行自我治疗。

sentences.en: Some of these have seen positive results, while others have experienced psychological turmoil.
sentences.zh: 其中一些人看到了积极的结果，而另一些人则经历了心理动荡。

blocks.html_en: “People’s expectations and hopes have far outstripped the evidence,” warns Hellerstein, adding that more rigorous studies are critical.

sentences.en: “People’s expectations and hopes have far outstripped the evidence,” warns Hellerstein, adding that more rigorous studies are critical.
sentences.zh: 海勒斯坦警告说：“人们的期望和希望远远超过了证据。”他补充说，更严格的研究至关重要。

blocks.html_en: For now, “there is hope” for people with eating disorders, says study co-author Hannah Douglass, a researcher at Imperial College London, who emphasizes that evidence-based care exists. “You can absolutely recover without psychedelics.”

sentences.en: For now, “there is hope” for people with eating disorders, says study co-author Hannah Douglass, a researcher at Imperial College London, who emphasizes that evidence-based care exists.
sentences.zh: 该研究的合著者、伦敦帝国理工学院的研究员汉娜·道格拉斯（Hannah Douglass）表示，目前饮食失调患者“还有希望”，她强调基于证据的护理是存在的。

sentences.en: “You can absolutely recover without psychedelics.”
sentences.zh: “不用迷幻药，你绝对可以康复。”

blocks.html_en: Shaking the “Snow Globe”

sentences.en: Shaking the “Snow Globe”
sentences.zh: 摇晃“雪球”

blocks.html_en: As it stands, recovery can be brutal. Eating disorders are particularly challenging to treat, in part because they are a “survival strategy,” Danby says—a coping mechanism for overwhelming situations. “The symptoms of anorexia are a language of pain,” explains Danby’s colleague Meg Vardy, a researcher and chairperson of the New Zealand–based eating disorder charity JourneyED Eating Disorder Support Aotearoa (the Māori name for New Zealand). The condition is rarely just about food or weight, but “something going on underneath.”

sentences.en: As it stands, recovery can be brutal.
sentences.zh: 就目前情况而言，复苏可能是残酷的。

sentences.en: Eating disorders are particularly challenging to treat, in part because they are a “survival strategy,” Danby says—a coping mechanism for overwhelming situations.
sentences.zh: 丹比说，饮食失调的治疗特别具有挑战性，部分原因是它们是一种“生存策略”——一种应对压倒性情况的机制。

sentences.en: “The symptoms of anorexia are a language of pain,” explains Danby’s colleague Meg Vardy, a researcher and chairperson of the New Zealand–based eating disorder charity JourneyED Eating Disorder Support Aotearoa (the Māori name for New Zealand).
sentences.zh: “厌食症的症状是一种痛苦的语言，”丹比的同事梅格·瓦尔迪 (Meg Vardy) 解释道，她是新西兰饮食失调慈善机构 JourneyED 饮食失调支持 Aotearoa（新西兰的毛利语名称）的研究员兼主席。

sentences.en: The condition is rarely just about food or weight, but “something going on underneath.”
sentences.zh: 这种情况很少与食物或体重有关，而是“内在发生的事情”。

blocks.html_en: Anorexia can provide comfort, control, a sense of order and something to fixate on, says trial participant Katharine. “It is very difficult to let go of because it is filling a hole.”

sentences.en: Anorexia can provide comfort, control, a sense of order and something to fixate on, says trial participant Katharine.
sentences.zh: 试验参与者凯瑟琳说，厌食症可以提供舒适感、控制力、秩序感和注意力。

sentences.en: “It is very difficult to let go of because it is filling a hole.”
sentences.zh: “放手是非常困难的，因为它正在填补一个洞。”

blocks.html_en: A starving or underweight brain also tends to become more rigid, “black and white” in its thinking, sensitive to fear and closed to change. Eating disorders are somewhat like obsessive-compulsive disorder or substance use disorder and involve brain circuits that are very resistant to intervention, Hellerstein says.

sentences.en: A starving or underweight brain also tends to become more rigid, “black and white” in its thinking, sensitive to fear and closed to change.
sentences.zh: 饥饿或体重不足的大脑也往往会变得更加僵化，思维变得“非黑即白”，对恐惧敏感，不愿改变。

sentences.en: Eating disorders are somewhat like obsessive-compulsive disorder or substance use disorder and involve brain circuits that are very resistant to intervention, Hellerstein says.
sentences.zh: 海勒斯坦说，饮食失调有点像强迫症或物质使用障碍，并且涉及非常难以干预的大脑回路。

blocks.html_en: Both animal and human studies suggest psychedelics could change brain function and increase cognitive flexibility, as well as emotional connectedness—features that tend to be impaired in people with eating disorders.

sentences.en: Both animal and human studies suggest psychedelics could change brain function and increase cognitive flexibility, as well as emotional connectedness—features that tend to be impaired in people with eating disorders.
sentences.zh: 动物和人类研究都表明，迷幻药可以改变大脑功能，提高认知灵活性以及情感联系——饮食失调患者的这些功能往往会受到损害。

blocks.html_en: Carhart-Harris likens psilocybin therapy to “shaking a snow globe.” The idea is to shake up and weaken potentially problematic thought patterns and introduce opportunities to do things differently, he says. In animal studies, psychedelics appear to induce a window of neuroplasticity, making the brain more malleable. “It can be an opportunity to regain agency [and] self-determination and not be a slave to habits that are strongly ingrained,” he says.

sentences.en: Carhart-Harris likens psilocybin therapy to “shaking a snow globe.”
sentences.zh: 卡哈特-哈里斯将裸盖菇素疗法比作“摇动雪球”。

sentences.en: The idea is to shake up and weaken potentially problematic thought patterns and introduce opportunities to do things differently, he says.
sentences.zh: 他说，这个想法是要动摇和削弱潜在有问题的思维模式，并引入以不同方式做事的机会。

sentences.en: In animal studies, psychedelics appear to induce a window of neuroplasticity, making the brain more malleable.
sentences.zh: 在动物研究中，迷幻药似乎能诱导神经可塑性窗口，使大脑更具可塑性。

sentences.en: “It can be an opportunity to regain agency [and] self-determination and not be a slave to habits that are strongly ingrained,” he says.
sentences.zh: “这可能是一个重新获得自主权和自决权的机会，而不是成为根深蒂固的习惯的奴隶，”他说。

blocks.html_en: That plasticity can go either way, however—positive change, a relapse risk or a period of destabilization that’s especially dangerous for anorexia, Finkelstein cautions. Combining the drug with talk therapy may be critical to its success: this isn't a “magic bullet,” Vardy says.

sentences.en: That plasticity can go either way, however—positive change, a relapse risk or a period of destabilization that’s especially dangerous for anorexia, Finkelstein cautions.
sentences.zh: 然而，芬克尔斯坦警告说，这种可塑性可以是任何一种方式——积极的变化、复发风险或一段对厌食症特别危险的不稳定时期。

sentences.en: Combining the drug with talk therapy may be critical to its success: this isn't a “magic bullet,” Vardy says.
sentences.zh: 瓦尔迪说，将药物与谈话疗法结合起来可能对其成功至关重要：这不是“灵丹妙药”。

blocks.html_en: Bypassing the “Thinking Brain”

sentences.en: Bypassing the “Thinking Brain”
sentences.zh: 绕过“思考大脑”

blocks.html_en: Katharine, who spent 15 years in and out of hospitals because of her anorexia, says her psilocybin therapy sessions were “completely extraordinary.”

sentences.en: Katharine, who spent 15 years in and out of hospitals because of her anorexia, says her psilocybin therapy sessions were “completely extraordinary.”
sentences.zh: 凯瑟琳因厌食症在医院进出 15 年，她说她的裸盖菇素治疗过程“完全不同寻常”。

blocks.html_en: During one dosing, she had a vision of skating on a lake: “My mind was on the sidelines, saying to my body, ‘You can just be free now. I’m not going to hold you back. Just go; fly,’” she says. “And there was this feeling of complete release. My body was free.”

sentences.en: During one dosing, she had a vision of skating on a lake: “My mind was on the sidelines, saying to my body, ‘You can just be free now.
sentences.zh: 在一次服药期间，她出现了在湖上滑冰的幻象：“我的思想在一旁，对我的身体说，‘你现在可以自由了。

sentences.en: I’m not going to hold you back.
sentences.zh: 我不会阻止你。

sentences.en: Just go; fly,’” she says.
sentences.zh: 就走吧；飞翔，”她说。

sentences.en: “And there was this feeling of complete release.
sentences.zh: “而且有一种完全释放的感觉。

sentences.en: My body was free.”
sentences.zh: 我的身体是自由的。”

blocks.html_en: “Anorexia keeps you small in many ways,” she says. “I reconnected with how it felt to be a human and alive and sad and happy and nourished. [In the trial], I realized that I am the source of my healing, my power and my own strength.”

sentences.en: “Anorexia keeps you small in many ways,” she says.
sentences.zh: “厌食症在很多方面都会让你变小，”她说。

sentences.en: “I reconnected with how it felt to be a human and alive and sad and happy and nourished. [In the trial], I realized that I am the source of my healing, my power and my own strength.”
sentences.zh: “我重新体会到作为一个人的感觉，活着，悲伤，快乐和滋养。[在审判中]，我意识到我是我的治愈、我的力量和我自己的力量的源泉。”

blocks.html_en: Psilocybin therapy is not without risks, and experts caution that it shouldn’t happen without specialized support. The process can be transcendent—and terrifying.

sentences.en: Psilocybin therapy is not without risks, and experts caution that it shouldn’t happen without specialized support.
sentences.zh: 裸盖菇素疗法并非没有风险，专家警告说，如果没有专门的支持，这种疗法不应该发生。

sentences.en: The process can be transcendent—and terrifying.
sentences.zh: 这个过程可能是超然的——而且是可怕的。

blocks.html_en: Trial participant Christina was “very nervous” going in, she recalls. She expected visions of “fluffy clouds, unicorns and rainbows.” Instead the sessions felt horrific.

sentences.en: Trial participant Christina was “very nervous” going in, she recalls.
sentences.zh: 试验参与者克里斯蒂娜回忆说，她在参加试验时“非常紧张”。

sentences.en: She expected visions of “fluffy clouds, unicorns and rainbows.”
sentences.zh: 她期待看到“蓬松的云彩、独角兽和彩虹”。

sentences.en: Instead the sessions felt horrific.
sentences.zh: 相反，会议感觉很可怕。

blocks.html_en: “All I could see was blood everywhere,” she says. “The therapists’ faces morphed, and I felt like I was surrounded by monsters. I thought, ‘Oh, my god, what have I done?’”

sentences.en: “All I could see was blood everywhere,” she says.
sentences.zh: “我只能看到到处都是血，”她说。

sentences.en: “The therapists’ faces morphed, and I felt like I was surrounded by monsters.
sentences.zh: “治疗师的脸发生了变化，我感觉自己被怪物包围了。

sentences.en: I thought, ‘Oh, my god, what have I done?’”
sentences.zh: 我想，‘天哪，我做了什么？’”

blocks.html_en: The drug’s action is “psychologically agitating,” Carhart-Harris says, and it can surface unpleasant content, thoughts or memories. It requires courage, he says, but can be incredibly transformative. “You can let go of these demons.”

sentences.en: The drug’s action is “psychologically agitating,” Carhart-Harris says, and it can surface unpleasant content, thoughts or memories.
sentences.zh: 卡哈特-哈里斯说，这种药物的作用是“心理上的激动”，它可能会浮现出不愉快的内容、想法或记忆。

sentences.en: It requires courage, he says, but can be incredibly transformative.
sentences.zh: 他说，这需要勇气，但可以带来难以置信的变革。

sentences.en: “You can let go of these demons.”
sentences.zh: “你可以放开这些恶魔了。”

blocks.html_en: Psychedelics also work in a somatic way, meaning they bypass the “thinking brain” to allow physical sensations to help guide emotional processing, Danby explains. That can be useful for eating disorders because people often disconnect from feelings such as hunger, thirst, fatigue and cold.

sentences.en: Psychedelics also work in a somatic way, meaning they bypass the “thinking brain” to allow physical sensations to help guide emotional processing, Danby explains.
sentences.zh: 丹比解释说，迷幻药也以躯体方式发挥作用，这意味着它们绕过“思考大脑”，让身体感觉帮助指导情绪处理。

sentences.en: That can be useful for eating disorders because people often disconnect from feelings such as hunger, thirst, fatigue and cold.
sentences.zh: 这对治疗饮食失调很有用，因为人们经常与饥饿、口渴、疲劳和寒冷等感觉脱节。

那是 2022 年，克里斯蒂娜别无选择。 这位当时 34 岁的伦敦人迫切希望治愈她的神经性厌食症，尽管这种疾病正在吞噬她。 在与这种疾病作斗争六年后，她尝试了各种形式的行为疗法和数月的住院治疗，但没有任何效果。 最糟糕的是，这种疾病让她无法入睡，消耗太多精力，无法爬楼梯或刷牙。 她需要彻底的修复。

“你变成了厌食症，”克里斯蒂娜（为保护隐私而化名）说。 “你周围没有生命。 你不笑。 你不笑。 你在任何事情中都找不到快乐，”她回忆道。 她的人际关系受到影响，她几乎失去了工作和房子。

最终，在谷歌上疯狂搜索“厌食症的治疗方法”，让她注意到一项用于治疗这种疾病的迷幻裸盖菇素（迷幻蘑菇的活性成分）的临床试验。 她报名了。

关于支持科学新闻

“我真诚地相信，如果我没有进行这项试验，我要么会被困在医院里，要么今天就不会在这里，”她说。 “它救了我的命。”

饮食失调的生活会将身心变成监狱。 侵入性的、永无休止的思维螺旋会导致强迫行为，例如暴饮暴食、过度运动、净化和限制饮食。 传统的精神科治疗，例如认知行为疗法或抗抑郁药物，仅对大约一半的患者有效。 厌食症患者死于自杀的可能性是一般人群的 18 倍以上，是所有精神疾病中死亡率最高的。

几十年来，研究人员一直在寻找更有效的疗法，但进展缓慢。 现在，科学家们正在转向更非正统的方法，包括裸盖菇素疗法。

从研究角度来看，现在还处于早期阶段。 尽管如此，2026 年可能是迷幻药的转折点。 特朗普政府敦促美国药品监管机构拥抱这一领域，并资助使用这些药物治疗心理健康状况的研究。 加州大学旧金山分校神经病学和精神病学杰出教授罗宾·卡哈特-哈里斯 (Robin Carhart-Harris) 预测，就裸盖菇素而言，美国食品和药物管理局可能会在五年内批准这种迷幻药用于治疗抑郁症或饮食失调。

“赛洛西宾疗法有可能阻止许多不必要的痛苦，”专门研究饮食失调的心理治疗师詹妮弗·丹比（Jennifer Danby）说。

裸盖菇素治疗过程中

裸盖菇素已显示出治疗创伤后应激障碍、抑郁症和其他精神疾病的潜力。 卡哈特-哈里斯说，人们有一种“直觉”，认为迷幻药也可以打破厌食症的心理障碍。

这一暗示，加上更广泛缺乏有效治疗方法，激发了一项涉及 21 名女性的小型试点试验。 参与者平均患有神经性厌食症 11 年。 在上个月发表的这项研究中，丹比和她的同事发现裸盖菇素与谈话疗法相结合，可以减轻厌食症状并增加参与者改变的动力。

该数据是在 2023 年《自然医学》杂志上发表的另一项小型研究之后发现的，该研究发现，每 10 名患有这种疾病的患者中，有 4 人在服用单剂量裸盖菇素后，其饮食失调评分显着下降。 如果在更大规模的试验中得到证实，这些结果表明裸盖菇素疗法可以启动厌食症的恢复并提供缓解。

2022 年，克里斯蒂娜加入了审判。 在六周的时间里，该小组接受了三剂口服裸盖菇素——首先是一毫克，然后是两剂 25 毫克，每剂间隔两周——同时在给药前后进行强化谈话治疗。 不良事件很少，只有 1 人退出研究；然而，另一名参与者两次试图自杀，研究小组称这些事件与试验无关。

这种裸盖菇素疗法与典型的饮食失调疗法有几个显着的不同：没有营养干预或专注于增加体重，研究人员没有看到参与者的体重指数发生有意义的变化。 相反，他们专注于自我同情并让家庭成员寻求支持。

研究人员在试验后两周、三个月、六个月和一年对参与者进行了随访。 他们发现，平均而言，参与者症状的严重程度有所减轻。 三个月后，一半的参与者在饮食失调症状测量方面的得分与未诊断的人相当。 参与者报告说，在试验结束后，恢复的动力持续了一年。

该研究的合著者卡哈特-哈里斯说：“这些人已经尝试了一切，但没有任何效果。” 其中一半人在三个月后病情得到缓解，这“令人印象深刻”。

“这项研究的结果意义深远，”澳大利亚斯威本科技大学临床心理学家克莱尔·芬克尔斯坦（Claire Finkelstein）说，她没有参与这项试验。 “但数据虽然很有希望，但也向我们表明，它并不适合所有人。 我们需要更多的研究来了解它对谁有帮助、为什么以及如何改善对那些没有反应的人的治疗。”

41 岁的试验参与者凯瑟琳 (Katharine) 患有严重厌食症 15 年，并要求在本文中只使用她的名字，对于她来说，裸盖菇素疗法并不是一根“魔杖”。 但随着时间的推移，她说，这次审判“在某种程度上让我心碎了”。

“有时我仍然会挣扎，但自从审判以来，我不会再将自己定义为厌食症患者，”她说。

哥伦比亚大学欧文医学中心临床精神病学教授大卫·海勒斯坦（David Hellerstein）并未参与这项研究，他认为，这些发现“有点令人鼓舞”，但也有一些警告。 由于没有对照组，因此很难知道裸盖菇素是否会产生影响。

试验研究人员表示，尽管如此，针对厌食症的有效治疗方法仍然很少，任何积极的信号都是有意义的。 “人们把厌食症比作慢性自杀，”卡哈特-哈里斯说。 “那种‘我想要活下去并且保持健康’的感觉是巨大的。”

一些患有饮食失调的人并没有等待药物批准或新法规；他们正在等待。他们已经通过地下渠道使用迷幻药进行自我治疗。 其中一些人看到了积极的结果，而另一些人则经历了心理动荡。

海勒斯坦警告说：“人们的期望和希望远远超过了证据。”他补充说，更严格的研究至关重要。

该研究的合著者、伦敦帝国理工学院的研究员汉娜·道格拉斯（Hannah Douglass）表示，目前饮食失调患者“还有希望”，她强调基于证据的护理是存在的。 “不用迷幻药，你绝对可以康复。”

摇晃“雪球”

就目前情况而言，复苏可能是残酷的。 丹比说，饮食失调的治疗特别具有挑战性，部分原因是它们是一种“生存策略”——一种应对压倒性情况的机制。 “厌食症的症状是一种痛苦的语言，”丹比的同事梅格·瓦尔迪 (Meg Vardy) 解释道，她是新西兰饮食失调慈善机构 JourneyED 饮食失调支持 Aotearoa（新西兰的毛利语名称）的研究员兼主席。 这种情况很少与食物或体重有关，而是“内在发生的事情”。

试验参与者凯瑟琳说，厌食症可以提供舒适感、控制力、秩序感和注意力。 “放手是非常困难的，因为它正在填补一个洞。”

饥饿或体重不足的大脑也往往会变得更加僵化，思维变得“非黑即白”，对恐惧敏感，不愿改变。 海勒斯坦说，饮食失调有点像强迫症或物质使用障碍，并且涉及非常难以干预的大脑回路。

动物和人类研究都表明，迷幻药可以改变大脑功能，提高认知灵活性以及情感联系——饮食失调患者的这些功能往往会受到损害。

卡哈特-哈里斯将裸盖菇素疗法比作“摇动雪球”。 他说，这个想法是要动摇和削弱潜在有问题的思维模式，并引入以不同方式做事的机会。 在动物研究中，迷幻药似乎能诱导神经可塑性窗口，使大脑更具可塑性。 “这可能是一个重新获得自主权和自决权的机会，而不是成为根深蒂固的习惯的奴隶，”他说。

然而，芬克尔斯坦警告说，这种可塑性可以是任何一种方式——积极的变化、复发风险或一段对厌食症特别危险的不稳定时期。 瓦尔迪说，将药物与谈话疗法结合起来可能对其成功至关重要：这不是“灵丹妙药”。

绕过“思考大脑”

凯瑟琳因厌食症在医院进出 15 年，她说她的裸盖菇素治疗过程“完全不同寻常”。

在一次服药期间，她出现了在湖上滑冰的幻象：“我的思想在一旁，对我的身体说，‘你现在可以自由了。 我不会阻止你。 就走吧；飞翔，”她说。 “而且有一种完全释放的感觉。 我的身体是自由的。”

“厌食症在很多方面都会让你变小，”她说。 “我重新体会到作为一个人的感觉，活着，悲伤，快乐和滋养。[在审判中]，我意识到我是我的治愈、我的力量和我自己的力量的源泉。”

裸盖菇素疗法并非没有风险，专家警告说，如果没有专门的支持，这种疗法不应该发生。 这个过程可能是超然的——而且是可怕的。

试验参与者克里斯蒂娜回忆说，她在参加试验时“非常紧张”。 她期待看到“蓬松的云彩、独角兽和彩虹”。 相反，会议感觉很可怕。

“我只能看到到处都是血，”她说。 “治疗师的脸发生了变化，我感觉自己被怪物包围了。 我想，‘天哪，我做了什么？’”

卡哈特-哈里斯说，这种药物的作用是“心理上的激动”，它可能会浮现出不愉快的内容、想法或记忆。 他说，这需要勇气，但可以带来难以置信的变革。 “你可以放开这些恶魔了。”

丹比解释说，迷幻药也以躯体方式发挥作用，这意味着它们绕过“思考大脑”，让身体感觉帮助指导情绪处理。 这对治疗饮食失调很有用，因为人们经常与饥饿、口渴、疲劳和寒冷等感觉脱节。

克里斯蒂娜说，尽管她在服用药物方面经历了不舒服的经历，但这次试验改变了她的生活。 她开始再次倾听自己的身体暗示，冒险并重新融入生活。

“就我的生活质量而言，这是无与伦比的，”克里斯蒂娜说。 “我又有感觉了。 我能取得今天的成绩，95% 都归功于这次审判。”
